name: Phase banner
summary: Use a phase banner to show that a service is in alpha or beta and give users a way to provide feedback.
whenToUse: Use when a public service is genuinely in alpha or beta and users should understand its development status.
Provide a working feedback route that the team monitors and can act on.
whenNotToUse: Do not use a phase banner as a substitute for explaining known limitations or service availability.
Do not retain an alpha or beta label after the service no longer meets that lifecycle stage.

anatomy.name: Banner container
anatomy.description: A govuk-phase-banner sits inside the standard width context near the top of the page.

anatomy.name: Phase tag
anatomy.description: A GOV.UK Tag contains the current phase label.

anatomy.name: Feedback message
anatomy.description: Short text explains that the service is developing and contains a feedback link.

variants.name: Alpha
variants.use: An alpha service being tested and iterated.

variants.name: Beta
variants.use: A beta service available to users while continuing to improve.

behaviour: No GOV.UK JavaScript module is required.
Place the banner consistently below the header or service navigation and before main content.
The feedback link must work without JavaScript.
accessibility: The phase is visible text inside the tag rather than a colour-only badge.
Use descriptive feedback-link text when the surrounding sentence would not be announced with it.
Preserve link focus and visited-state behaviour.
content: Use the actual service phase label, usually “Alpha” or “Beta”.
Keep the message short and explain that feedback helps improve the service.
Link directly to the feedback mechanism rather than a generic homepage.

htmlExamples.name: Alpha phase banner
htmlExamples.html: Alpha This is a new service – your feedback will help us to improve it.
